structural_composition_rule: Owned event IDs and provenance.source_ids are deterministic unions of already accepted event/anchor/lifecycle/patch evidence. They make no new historical claim.

entries.named_predecessor: 1967 Bell floating-gate research, earlier mask ROM and one-time programmable memories, and MNOS charge-trap memories
entries.material_delta: The marketed Intel configuration combines electrical programming with ultraviolet whole-device erasure for repeated programming.
entries.locator: Floating gate, MNOS and Intel EPROM sections
entries.limits: Earlier nonvolatile and electrically alterable memories existed; no direct Bell-to-Intel influence is asserted.

entries.named_predecessor: Sharp CX-3 stationary-head digital Compact Cassette prototype in 1983; stationary and rotary DAT development; marketed rotary DAT and contemporaneous recordable MiniDisc
entries.material_delta: DCC used lossy PASC coding at 384 kbit/s, nine tracks per direction and analogue-recording playback. Sharp reported 14-bit 44.1 kHz stereo PCM and an 18-track head; the raw audio samples amount to 1.2348 Mbit/s before coding overhead. PASC trades exact sample preservation for a lower coded audio rate.
entries.locator: Printed p. 12; dcc-sharp1983 p. 42; dcc-standard PDF pp. 1–3; dcc-dat p. 17
entries.limits: The computed CX-3 sample rate is not an on-tape channel-rate measurement. Analogue-recording playback and sale of CX-3 are not established; no first compatibility, numerical cost saving or universal fidelity superiority is claimed. Tape seek time remains a tradeoff against random-access disc.

entries.named_predecessor: BBN PDP-1 protected interactive time sharing operational in 1962; earlier single-user interactive systems
entries.material_delta: The documented 1963 CTSS configuration combined named persistent user disk files and compatible batch service with interactive shared access.
entries.locator: Printed pp. 51–52, 56; ctss-bbn pp. 140–141; ctss-manual pp. 23–24; ctss-mac Summer Study
entries.limits: Protected time sharing and file systems did not originate with CTSS; the comparison is to named predecessors and does not establish universal priority.

entries.named_predecessor: INGRES multi-variable decomposition, January 1976 minimum-cost recurrence and smallest-relation heuristic
entries.material_delta: System R implemented subset join enumeration retaining plans with useful orderings and using catalog statistics plus estimated CPU and I/O costs.
entries.locator: Section 7, printed pp. 21–24 / PDF pp. 23–26; sysr-opt pp. 23–34
entries.limits: Cost-based reasoning predates this implementation; no universal first query optimization or nonprocedural language claim.

entries.named_predecessor: System R shadow-page recovery and DB2 write-ahead/page/compensation logging, including partial rollback
entries.material_delta: ARIES chains redo-only compensation records using UndoNxtLSN to skip already-undone actions and bound rollback logging through repeated failures, unlike the earlier compared DB2 behavior.
entries.locator: Printed pp. 109–110; aries-db2 pp. 182–183; aries-exodus pp. 166–168
entries.limits: DB2 already had compensation records and internal partial rollback. EXODUS adapted ARIES and used page-or-coarser data locks; no record-level locking or complete product implementation is inferred.

entries.named_predecessor: Commercial MOS photodiode arrays, including 50×50 cameras; Sangster/Teer bucket-brigade charge transfer and proposed imaging
entries.material_delta: Charge-coupled potential wells transport image charge without a separate transfer transistor at each stage, a distinct imaging architecture with noise and transfer-loss tradeoffs.
entries.limits: Not first solid-state imaging or first analog charge transfer; 1973 video performance projections are not attributed to the offered linear device.

frontier_scope: Exact independently reviewed configuration comparisons. Only accepted proposed records enter the canonical graph; held leads and excluded candidates in supporting context are unresolved research, not additional accepted facts. No exhaustive worldwide priority survey is claimed.
